what: This is a preferred share of Huntington Bancshares, the Ohio regional bank. It pays a fixed dividend, ranks ahead of the bank's ordinary shares, and does not participate in the bank's growth.
customers: The bank serves Midwestern households and businesses; this security is bought by investors who want a fixed payment.
money: deposits, mortgages, car and equipment lending
corporate lending, treasury management and specialty finance
moat: The bank's deposit base across Ohio and Michigan, built since 1866, funds lending cheaply and generates the earnings behind this payment.
risks: The dividend is declared at the board's discretion and can be suspended
It ranks behind all of the bank's debt
Its market price falls when long-term interest rates rise
A severe credit downturn would eventually threaten the payment
opportunities: A yield well above the bank's ordinary shares
Paid before ordinary shareholders receive anything
The bank's net margin of 27% gives comfortable coverage
watch: Huntington's capital ratios and credit losses, and continued declaration of the dividend.
